explanation.si: kilo යනු මූලික ඒකකයේ 1,000 ගුණයකි.
explanation.technicalNoteJa: kilo＝1,000倍

questionText.en: Deci means one hundredth of a unit.
questionText.ja: deci（デシ）は<ruby>基本単位<rt>[object Object]</rt></ruby>の10分の1です。

questions.statement: deci（デシ）は<ruby>基本単位<rt>[object Object]</rt></ruby>の10分の1です。

explanation.en: Deci means one tenth; centi means one hundredth.
explanation.si: deci යනු දහයෙන් එකකි; සියයෙන් එක centi වේ.
explanation.technicalNoteJa: deci＝10分の1、centi＝100分の1

questionText.en: One millilitre may also be called one cubic centimetre.
questionText.ja: 1mLは1cc（<ruby>立方<rt>[object Object]</rt></ruby>センチメートル）ともいいます。

questions.statement: 1mLは1cc（<ruby>立方<rt>[object Object]</rt></ruby>センチメートル）ともいいます。

explanation.en: The source equates 1 mL with 1 cc.
explanation.si: 1 mL යන්න 1 cc ලෙසද හඳුන්වයි.
explanation.technicalNoteJa: 1mL＝1cc

questionText.en: One traditional Japanese shō equals 18 litres.
questionText.ja: 1<ruby>升<rt>[object Object]</rt></ruby>は1.8Lです。

questions.statement: 1<ruby>升<rt>[object Object]</rt></ruby>は1.8Lです。

explanation.en: One shō is 1.8 L; one tō is 18 L.
explanation.si: shō එකක් ලීටර් 1.8කි; tō එකක් ලීටර් 18කි.

questionText.en: Ten shō make one tō.
questionText.ja: 1<ruby>斗<rt>[object Object]</rt></ruby>は10<ruby>升<rt>[object Object]</rt></ruby>です。

questions.statement: 1<ruby>斗<rt>[object Object]</rt></ruby>は10<ruby>升<rt>[object Object]</rt></ruby>です。

explanation.en: The source gives 1 tō = 10 shō = 18 L.
explanation.si: 1 tō = shō 10ක් = ලීටර් 18කි.

questionText.en: Specific gravity is compared using water as the reference value 1.
questionText.ja: <ruby>比重<rt>[object Object]</rt></ruby>は、水を1として比べた<ruby>重さ<rt>[object Object]</rt></ruby>の割合です。

questions.statement: <ruby>比重<rt>[object Object]</rt></ruby>は、水を1として比べた<ruby>重さ<rt>[object Object]</rt></ruby>の割合です。

explanation.en: Specific gravity is relative to water, taken as 1.
explanation.si: සාපේක්ෂ ඝනත්වය ජලය 1 ලෙස සලකා සසඳයි.
explanation.technicalNoteJa: 比重＝水を1とした割合

questionText.en: For non-water materials, weight is calculated as volume divided by specific gravity.
questionText.ja: <ruby>水以外<rt>[object Object]</rt></ruby>の<ruby>物<rt>[object Object]</rt></ruby>の<ruby>重さ<rt>[object Object]</rt></ruby>は、<ruby>体積<rt>[object Object]</rt></ruby>×<ruby>比重<rt>[object Object]</rt></ruby>で計算します。

questions.statement: <ruby>水以外<rt>[object Object]</rt></ruby>の<ruby>物<rt>[object Object]</rt></ruby>の<ruby>重さ<rt>[object Object]</rt></ruby>は、<ruby>体積<rt>[object Object]</rt></ruby>×<ruby>比重<rt>[object Object]</rt></ruby>で計算します。

explanation.en: The formula is volume multiplied by specific gravity.
explanation.si: ජලය නොවන ද්‍රව්‍යයක බර = පරිමාව × සාපේක්ෂ ඝනත්වයයි.
explanation.technicalNoteJa: 重さ＝体積×比重

questionText.en: A volume of 0.5 m³ at specific gravity 0.9 weighs 0.45 tonnes.

explanation.en: The source example calculates 0.45 t, or 450 kg.

questionText.en: One traditional Japanese kan is approximately 3.75 kg.
questionText.ja: 1<ruby>貫<rt>[object Object]</rt></ruby>は<ruby>約<rt>[object Object]</rt></ruby>3.75kgです。

questions.statement: 1<ruby>貫<rt>[object Object]</rt></ruby>は<ruby>約<rt>[object Object]</rt></ruby>3.75kgです。

explanation.en: The source gives one kan as approximately 3.75 kg.
explanation.si: kan එකක් කිලෝග්‍රෑම් 3.75ක් පමණ වේ.

questionText.en: The measurement-tonne conversion uses 40 cubic feet as one tonne.
questionText.ja: <ruby>容積<rt>[object Object]</rt></ruby>トンは40<ruby>立方<rt>[object Object]</rt></ruby>フィートを1トンとして計算します。

questions.statement: <ruby>容積<rt>[object Object]</rt></ruby>トンは40<ruby>立方<rt>[object Object]</rt></ruby>フィートを1トンとして計算します。

explanation.en: The source states 40 cubic feet (1.133 m³) = 1 measurement tonne.
explanation.si: cubic feet 40ක් (1.133 m³) = measurement tonne 1කි.
explanation.technicalNoteJa: 40立方フィート＝1容積トン

questionText.en: Effective height is limited by the lower of the main beam underside or duct bottom.
questionText.ja: <ruby>有効高<rt>[object Object]</rt></ruby>は、<ruby>大梁<rt>[object Object]</rt></ruby>の下またはダクトの<ruby>下端<rt>[object Object]</rt></ruby>の<ruby>低い方<rt>[object Object]</rt></ruby>までです。

questions.statement: <ruby>有効高<rt>[object Object]</rt></ruby>は、<ruby>大梁<rt>[object Object]</rt></ruby>の下またはダクトの<ruby>下端<rt>[object Object]</rt></ruby>の<ruby>低い方<rt>[object Object]</rt></ruby>までです。

explanation.en: Use the lower obstruction to determine usable cargo height.
explanation.si: භාණ්ඩ තැබිය හැකි උස තීරණය වන්නේ beam පහළ හෝ duct පහළ යන දෙකෙන් අඩු අගය අනුවය.
explanation.technicalNoteJa: 有効高＝大梁下またはダクト下端の低い方

questionText.en: The refrigerated-warehouse equipment-tonnage formula includes factors 0.9 and 0.4.
questionText.ja: <ruby>設備<rt>[object Object]</rt></ruby>トン＝<ruby>床面積<rt>[object Object]</rt></ruby>×<ruby>有効高<rt>[object Object]</rt></ruby>×0.9×0.4です。

questions.statement: <ruby>設備<rt>[object Object]</rt></ruby>トン＝<ruby>床面積<rt>[object Object]</rt></ruby>×<ruby>有効高<rt>[object Object]</rt></ruby>×0.9×0.4です。

explanation.en: The formula multiplies floor area and effective height by 0.9 and 0.4.
explanation.si: සූත්‍රයට 0.9 සහ 0.4 ගුණක දෙකම ඇතුළත් වේ.
explanation.technicalNoteJa: 床面積×有効高×0.9×0.4

questionText.en: A thermometer and hygrometer are used to measure temperature and humidity.
questionText.ja: <ruby>温度計<rt>[object Object]</rt></ruby>と<ruby>湿度計<rt>[object Object]</rt></ruby>で<ruby>温度<rt>[object Object]</rt></ruby>と<ruby>湿度<rt>[object Object]</rt></ruby>を<ruby>測定<rt>[object Object]</rt></ruby>します。

questions.statement: <ruby>温度計<rt>[object Object]</rt></ruby>と<ruby>湿度計<rt>[object Object]</rt></ruby>で<ruby>温度<rt>[object Object]</rt></ruby>と<ruby>湿度<rt>[object Object]</rt></ruby>を<ruby>測定<rt>[object Object]</rt></ruby>します。

explanation.en: The source names these two measuring instruments.
explanation.si: උෂ්ණත්වය සහ ආර්ද්‍රතාව මැනීමට thermometer සහ hygrometer භාවිත කරයි.
explanation.technicalNoteJa: 温度計・湿度計

questionText.en: The ordinary-work illumination standard is at least 150 lux.
questionText.ja: <ruby>普通作業<rt>[object Object]</rt></ruby>の<ruby>明るさ<rt>[object Object]</rt></ruby>の<ruby>基準<rt>[object Object]</rt></ruby>は150lx<ruby>以上<rt>[object Object]</rt></ruby>です。

questions.statement: <ruby>普通作業<rt>[object Object]</rt></ruby>の<ruby>明るさ<rt>[object Object]</rt></ruby>の<ruby>基準<rt>[object Object]</rt></ruby>は150lx<ruby>以上<rt>[object Object]</rt></ruby>です。

explanation.en: The source states 150 lx or more.
explanation.si: සාමාන්‍ය වැඩ සඳහා අවම ආලෝකය 150 lx වේ.
explanation.technicalNoteJa: 普通作業＝150lx以上

questionText.en: In 24-hour notation, 11 p.m. is written as 11:00.
questionText.ja: 24<ruby>時間表記<rt>[object Object]</rt></ruby>では、<ruby>午後<rt>[object Object]</rt></ruby>11<ruby>時<rt>[object Object]</rt></ruby>は23:00です。

questions.statement: 24<ruby>時間表記<rt>[object Object]</rt></ruby>では、<ruby>午後<rt>[object Object]</rt></ruby>11<ruby>時<rt>[object Object]</rt></ruby>は23:00です。

explanation.en: 11 p.m. is 23:00 in 24-hour format.
explanation.si: 24-hour ක්‍රමයේ රාත්‍රී 11 යනු 23:00 වේ.

questionText.en: Japanese counters are selected according to an item's shape or nature.
questionText.ja: <ruby>助数詞<rt>[object Object]</rt></ruby>は、<ruby>物<rt>[object Object]</rt></ruby>の<ruby>形<rt>[object Object]</rt></ruby>や<ruby>性質<rt>[object Object]</rt></ruby>によって<ruby>使い分け<rt>[object Object]</rt></ruby>ます。

questions.statement: <ruby>助数詞<rt>[object Object]</rt></ruby>は、<ruby>物<rt>[object Object]</rt></ruby>の<ruby>形<rt>[object Object]</rt></ruby>や<ruby>性質<rt>[object Object]</rt></ruby>によって<ruby>使い分け<rt>[object Object]</rt></ruby>ます。

explanation.en: Counters vary with the shape and characteristics of the item.
explanation.si: භාණ්ඩයේ හැඩය හා ස්වභාවය අනුව counter තෝරයි.
explanation.technicalNoteJa: 助数詞は形や性質で使い分ける

questionText.en: The counter 本 is used for flat, thin items such as corrugated sheets.
questionText.ja: 枚は、<ruby>段<rt>[object Object]</rt></ruby>ボールのような<ruby>平たく<rt>[object Object]</rt></ruby><ruby>薄い<rt>[object Object]</rt></ruby><ruby>物<rt>[object Object]</rt></ruby>に使います。

questions.statement: 枚は、<ruby>段<rt>[object Object]</rt></ruby>ボールのような<ruby>平たく<rt>[object Object]</rt></ruby><ruby>薄い<rt>[object Object]</rt></ruby><ruby>物<rt>[object Object]</rt></ruby>に使います。

explanation.en: 枚 is for flat thin objects; 本 is for long slender objects.
explanation.si: පැතලි තුනී දේ සඳහා 枚 ද දිගු සිහින් දේ සඳහා 本 ද භාවිත කරයි.
explanation.technicalNoteJa: 枚＝平たく薄い物／本＝細長い物

questionText.en: The counter 台 is used for machinery and equipment such as forklifts.
questionText.ja: フォークリフトなどの<ruby>機械<rt>[object Object]</rt></ruby>・<ruby>設備<rt>[object Object]</rt></ruby>には台を使います。

questions.statement: フォークリフトなどの<ruby>機械<rt>[object Object]</rt></ruby>・<ruby>設備<rt>[object Object]</rt></ruby>には台を使います。

explanation.en: 台 is used for machinery and equipment, including forklifts.
explanation.si: Forklift වැනි යන්ත්‍ර ගණන් කිරීමට 台 භාවිත කරයි.
explanation.technicalNoteJa: 台＝機械・設備

questionText.en: The counter 冊 is used for books and booklets.
questionText.ja: <ruby>本<rt>[object Object]</rt></ruby>や<ruby>冊子<rt>[object Object]</rt></ruby>には冊を使います。

questions.statement: <ruby>本<rt>[object Object]</rt></ruby>や<ruby>冊子<rt>[object Object]</rt></ruby>には冊を使います。

explanation.en: 冊 is used for books and booklets.
explanation.si: පොත් සහ පොත් පිංච සඳහා 冊 භාවිත කරයි.
explanation.technicalNoteJa: 冊＝本・冊子

questionText.en: The counter 足 is used for clothing items.
questionText.ja: 着は<ruby>衣類<rt>[object Object]</rt></ruby>、足は<ruby>靴<rt>[object Object]</rt></ruby>などの<ruby>履物<rt>[object Object]</rt></ruby>に使います。

questions.statement: 着は<ruby>衣類<rt>[object Object]</rt></ruby>、足は<ruby>靴<rt>[object Object]</rt></ruby>などの<ruby>履物<rt>[object Object]</rt></ruby>に使います。

explanation.en: 着 is for clothing; 足 is for footwear.
explanation.si: ඇඳුම් සඳහා 着 ද පාවහන් සඳහා 足 ද භාවිත කරයි.
explanation.technicalNoteJa: 着＝衣類／足＝履物

questionText.en: The counter か所 is used to count locations.
questionText.ja: <ruby>場所<rt>[object Object]</rt></ruby>の<ruby>数<rt>[object Object]</rt></ruby>には「か所」を使います。

questions.statement: <ruby>場所<rt>[object Object]</rt></ruby>の<ruby>数<rt>[object Object]</rt></ruby>には「か所」を使います。

explanation.en: か所 is used to count locations.
explanation.si: ස්ථාන ගණන සඳහා か所 භාවිත කරයි.
explanation.technicalNoteJa: か所＝場所の数

questionText.en: A reusable transport item may be a standard-sized plastic container used repeatedly in logistics.
questionText.ja: <ruby>RTIは、物流で繰り返し使う決まった大きさのプラスチック容器です。</ruby>

questions.statement: <ruby>RTIは、物流で繰り返し使う決まった大きさのプラスチック容器です。</ruby>

explanation.en: RTI is a reusable logistics container, often a standard-sized plastic box.
explanation.si: RTI යනු logistics කටයුතු සඳහා නැවත නැවත භාවිත කරන නියමිත ප්‍රමාණයේ ප්ලාස්ටික් බහාලුමකි.
explanation.technicalNoteJa: RTI＝リターナブル物流容器

questionText.en: When cargo quantity differs from documents, the discrepancy should be recorded with the driver present and the driver's signature obtained.
questionText.ja: <ruby>数量が違うときは、ドライバー立会いで内容を記録し、署名をもらいます。</ruby>

questions.statement: <ruby>数量が違うときは、ドライバー立会いで内容を記録し、署名をもらいます。</ruby>

explanation.en: The source requires documenting the discrepancy with the driver present and obtaining a signature.
explanation.si: භාණ්ඩ ප්‍රමාණය ලේඛනවලින් වෙනස් නම් රියදුරු ඉදිරියේ විස්තර සටහන් කර අත්සන ලබාගත යුතුය.
explanation.technicalNoteJa: 数量違い＝立会い記録・署名

questionText.en: Visible external damage always proves that the cargo inside is undamaged.
questionText.ja: <ruby>外観に傷がある場合、内部にも不良がある可能性があります。</ruby>

questions.statement: <ruby>外観に傷がある場合、内部にも不良がある可能性があります。</ruby>

explanation.en: External damage may indicate internal defects; it does not prove the contents are sound.
explanation.si: පිටතින් හානි පෙනේ නම් ඇතුළත භාණ්ඩවලටද හානි වී තිබිය හැකිය.
explanation.technicalNoteJa: 外観の損傷は内部不良の可能性

questionText.en: The remark code WET indicates that cargo or its packaging is wet.
questionText.ja: <ruby>WETは、貨物や包装が濡れていることを示します。</ruby>

questions.statement: <ruby>WETは、貨物や包装が濡れていることを示します。</ruby>

explanation.en: WET is one of the listed cargo-condition remarks.
explanation.si: WET යනු භාණ්ඩය හෝ ඇසුරුම තෙත් වී ඇති බව දක්වන සටහනකි.
explanation.technicalNoteJa: WET＝濡れている

questionText.en: The remark code BANDS OFF means that the cargo has leaked.
questionText.ja: <ruby>BANDS OFFは、バンドが切れたり外れたりした状態です。</ruby>

questions.statement: <ruby>BANDS OFFは、バンドが切れたり外れたりした状態です。</ruby>

explanation.en: BANDS OFF refers to broken or missing bands; LEAKING means leakage.
explanation.si: BANDS OFF යනු බැඳුම් පටි කැඩී හෝ ගැලවී ඇති බවයි; කාන්දු වීම LEAKING වේ.
explanation.technicalNoteJa: BANDS OFF＝バンド切れ

questionText.en: If a barcode cannot be read, the worker should report it to the supervisor and follow instructions.
questionText.ja: <ruby>バーコードが読めない場合は、責任者に報告して指示に従います。</ruby>

questions.statement: <ruby>バーコードが読めない場合は、責任者に報告して指示に従います。</ruby>

explanation.en: Unreadable barcodes must be escalated to the supervisor.
explanation.si: Barcode එක කියවිය නොහැකි නම් වගකිවයුතු නිලධාරියාට දන්වා උපදෙස් අනුව ක්‍රියා කළ යුතුය.
explanation.technicalNoteJa: バーコード不読＝責任者へ報告

questionText.en: Warehouse locations are managed using letters and numbers.
questionText.ja: <ruby>倉庫のロケーションは、英字と数字で管理します。</ruby>

questions.statement: <ruby>倉庫のロケーションは、英字と数字で管理します。</ruby>

explanation.en: The source describes a location as a warehouse address managed alphanumerically.
explanation.si: ගබඩා location අකුරු සහ ඉලක්කම් භාවිතයෙන් පාලනය කරයි.
explanation.technicalNoteJa: ロケーション＝英数字で管理

questionText.en: A fixed-location system allows any cargo to be placed in any empty slot without a preassigned location.
questionText.ja: <ruby>固定ロケーションでは、貨物ごとに決まった保管場所があります。</ruby>

questions.statement: <ruby>固定ロケーションでは、貨物ごとに決まった保管場所があります。</ruby>

explanation.en: Fixed location assigns a regular place to each cargo type; free location uses any available slot.
explanation.si: Fixed location ක්‍රමයේදී භාණ්ඩ වර්ගයට නියමිත ස්ථානයක් ඇත; හිස් ඕනෑම තැනක තැබීම free location වේ.
explanation.technicalNoteJa: 固定ロケーション＝決まった場所

questionText.en: A disadvantage of free-location storage is that finding the exact stock location can take effort.
questionText.ja: <ruby>フリーロケーションでは、貨物の場所を確認するのに手間がかかります。</ruby>

questions.statement: <ruby>フリーロケーションでは、貨物の場所を確認するのに手間がかかります。</ruby>

explanation.en: Free location improves space use but can require effort to locate stock.
explanation.si: Free location ක්‍රමයෙන් ඉඩකඩ හොඳින් භාවිත කළ හැකි නමුත් තොගය සොයාගැනීමට වැඩි කාලයක් ගත විය හැකිය.
explanation.technicalNoteJa: フリーロケーション＝所在確認に手間

questionText.en: In double-transaction storage, both the picking area and bulk stock area are managed as fixed locations.
questionText.ja: <ruby>ダブルトランザクションでは、ピッキングエリアは固定、ストックエリアはフリーです。</ruby>

questions.statement: <ruby>ダブルトランザクションでは、ピッキングエリアは固定、ストックエリアはフリーです。</ruby>

explanation.en: The picking area is fixed while the stock area is free.
explanation.si: Double transaction ක්‍රමයේ picking area එක fixed වන අතර stock area එක free වේ.
explanation.technicalNoteJa: ピッキング＝固定／ストック＝フリー

questionText.en: Double-transaction storage requires replenishment from the stock area to the picking area.
questionText.ja: <ruby>ダブルトランザクションでは、ストックエリアからピッキングエリアへの補充が必要です。</ruby>

questions.statement: <ruby>ダブルトランザクションでは、ストックエリアからピッキングエリアへの補充が必要です。</ruby>

explanation.en: The method improves picking efficiency but requires replenishment.
explanation.si: මෙම ක්‍රමය picking කාර්යක්ෂමතාව වැඩි කළත් stock area එකෙන් picking area එකට නැවත භාණ්ඩ පිරවීම අවශ්‍ය වේ.
explanation.technicalNoteJa: 補充＝ストックからピッキングへ

questionText.en: A sashifuda is a card that records cargo details and inbound/outbound movements.
questionText.ja: <ruby>さし札は、貨物明細と入出庫記録を書く札です。</ruby>

questions.statement: <ruby>さし札は、貨物明細と入出庫記録を書く札です。</ruby>

explanation.en: The stock card records cargo details and inbound/outbound records.
explanation.si: Sashifuda යනු භාණ්ඩ විස්තර සහ ඇතුළත්/පිටත් කිරීමේ සටහන් ලියන කාඩ්පතකි.
explanation.technicalNoteJa: さし札＝貨物明細・入出庫記録

questionText.en: If picked stock is insufficient, the worker may independently change the quantity written on the release instruction.
questionText.ja: <ruby>欠品があれば事務所に報告し、指示書の数字を自分で修正してはいけません。</ruby>

questions.statement: <ruby>欠品があれば事務所に報告し、指示書の数字を自分で修正してはいけません。</ruby>

explanation.en: A shortage must be reported; workers must not alter the instruction quantity themselves.
explanation.si: තොගය අඩු නම් කාර්යාලයට වාර්තා කළ යුතුය; උපදෙස් පත්‍රයේ ප්‍රමාණය තමන්ම වෙනස් නොකළ යුතුය.
explanation.technicalNoteJa: 欠品＝報告／指図書を自分で修正しない

questionText.en: Single picking gathers goods separately for each delivery destination.
questionText.ja: <ruby>シングルピッキングは、出荷先ごとに貨物を集めます。</ruby>

questions.statement: <ruby>シングルピッキングは、出荷先ごとに貨物を集めます。</ruby>

explanation.en: Single/order picking gathers goods separately by destination.
explanation.si: Single picking ක්‍රමයේදී එක් එක් delivery destination සඳහා භාණ්ඩ වෙන වෙනම එකතු කරයි.
explanation.technicalNoteJa: シングルピッキング＝出荷先別

questionText.en: Total picking collects the required goods together first and sorts them by destination afterward.
questionText.ja: <ruby>トータルピッキングは、商品を一度に集めてから出荷先別に仕分けます。</ruby>

questions.statement: <ruby>トータルピッキングは、商品を一度に集めてから出荷先別に仕分けます。</ruby>

explanation.en: Total picking reduces travel by collecting goods together before destination sorting.
explanation.si: Total picking ක්‍රමයේදී අවශ්‍ය භාණ්ඩ එකවර එකතු කර පසුව ගමනාන්ත අනුව වෙන් කරයි.
explanation.technicalNoteJa: トータルピッキング＝一括収集後に仕分け

questionText.en: Sticker picking can allow inspection to take place at the same time as picking.
questionText.ja: <ruby>シールピッキングでは、ピッキングと同時に検品できます。</ruby>

questions.statement: <ruby>シールピッキングでは、ピッキングと同時に検品できます。</ruby>

explanation.en: The label is attached as each item is picked, enabling simultaneous checking.
explanation.si: Sticker picking කිරීමේදී භාණ්ඩය ගන්නා විටම label අලවන නිසා inspection එකද එකවර කළ හැකිය.
explanation.technicalNoteJa: シールピッキング＝ピッキングと検品

questionText.en: Outbound inspection should be checked by a second person as a double-check.
questionText.ja: <ruby>出庫検品では、別の人によるダブルチェックを行います。</ruby>

questions.statement: <ruby>出庫検品では、別の人によるダブルチェックを行います。</ruby>

explanation.en: The source calls for a second person's double-check.
explanation.si: Outbound inspection එකේදී වෙනත් සේවකයෙකු ලවා දෙවන පරීක්ෂාවක් කළ යුතුය.
explanation.technicalNoteJa: ダブルチェック＝別の人が確認

questionText.en: If damaged cargo is found and no instruction can be obtained from the depositor, the source says to handle it as a separate LOT.
questionText.ja: <ruby>寄託者の指示が得られなければ、別LOTとして扱います。</ruby>

questions.statement: <ruby>寄託者の指示が得られなければ、別LOTとして扱います。</ruby>

explanation.en: The source specifies separate-LOT handling if instructions cannot be obtained.
explanation.si: භාණ්ඩ හිමිකරුගෙන් උපදෙස් ලබාගත නොහැකි නම් හානි වූ භාණ්ඩ වෙනම LOT එකක් ලෙස සැලකිය යුතුය.
explanation.technicalNoteJa: 指示なし＝別LOT扱い

questionText.en: On a cage trolley, heavy and strong cartons should be placed below bags and crushable goods.
questionText.ja: <ruby>カゴ台車では、重く丈夫な箱を下に置き、袋物や潰れやすい物を上に置きます。</ruby>

questions.statement: <ruby>カゴ台車では、重く丈夫な箱を下に置き、袋物や潰れやすい物を上に置きます。</ruby>

explanation.en: The source recommends heavy, strong cartons at the bottom and crushable goods above.
explanation.si: Cage trolley එකක බර සහ ශක්තිමත් පෙට්ටි පහළින්ද පහසුවෙන් පොඩි වන බෑග්/භාණ්ඩ ඉහළින්ද තැබිය යුතුය.
explanation.technicalNoteJa: 重く丈夫な箱＝下／潰れやすい物＝上

questionText.en: Overhang means cargo extends beyond the edge of a pallet or the lower cargo.
questionText.ja: <ruby>貨物がパレットの端や下段からはみ出すことをオーバーハングといいます。</ruby>

questions.statement: <ruby>貨物がパレットの端や下段からはみ出すことをオーバーハングといいます。</ruby>

explanation.en: Overhang describes cargo projecting beyond the pallet edge or lower load.
explanation.si: භාණ්ඩ pallet එකේ අගින් හෝ පහළ භාණ්ඩවලින් පිටතට නෙරා යාම overhang ලෙස හැඳින්වේ.
explanation.technicalNoteJa: オーバーハング＝はみ出し
